I taught you literally everything.
Stop shouting across the whole hallway.
And you turned out to be an ungrateful woman!

meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Comparative of много. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.
Comparative of большой. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: They beat me literally every day!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: steadfast in allegiance or affection

examples.text: Ты мой главный учитель и верный наставник.
examples.trans: You are my main teacher and true mentor.

examples.text: А я вообще очень верная женщина.
examples.trans: And I am actually a very loyal woman.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: to bring up, to raise (a child)
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'спитывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bring up, to raise', paired with 'воспитать'.

examples.text: Марина, преподаватель. Разведена, воспитывает больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: Marina, a lecturer. Divorced, raising a sick child.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'door' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The door is behind the wardrobe.
Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: He talks for a long time.
We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

meanings.note: Contrast дома = at home. Core Russian adv meaning '(to) home, homeward' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
examples.trans: Your wife is a very wise woman. You listen to her.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Animate masculine noun. Common masculine noun meaning 'commander, commanding officer' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Speak, where is your uncle? Where is the commander?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'corridor, hall' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Who was that guy in the corridor?
He is standing in the long corridor.
As you can see, a big hall.

meanings.note: Кричать на + accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to shout', paired with 'крикнуть'.

examples.text: Не надо кричать. Хорошо, я буду сегодня.
examples.trans: There's no need to shout. All right, I'll be there tonight.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
+ prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'благодарный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ungrateful').

examples.text: Послушай, не клади трубку! Ах ты, неблагодарная!
examples.trans: Listen, don't hang up! Oh, you ungrateful girl!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'offense, resentment, hurt' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I will not forget this insult.
She was left with bitter resentment.

examples.text: Я всё равно не забуду эту обиду.
examples.trans: I will not forget this insult anyway.

meanings.note: Transitive verb. Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'учать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to teach, train', paired with 'обучить'.
Surprise, fright or pain. Core Russian interj meaning 'oh' in everyday speech.

оказаться.gloss: to turn out to be, find oneself

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be
meanings.note: Reflexive verb. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out to be, find oneself', paired with 'оказываться'.

examples.trans: You turned out to be ungrateful.

examples.text: Он внезапно оказался в центре событий.
examples.trans: He suddenly found himself in the center of events.
And you turned out to be an ungrateful woman!

meanings.note: Её, ей, ей, о ней. Core Russian pron meaning 'she; it' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Often with annoyance. Core Russian adv meaning 'again' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: A door, a window. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to open', paired with 'открывать'.

examples.trans: Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: перестань(те)! = stop it!, oh come on!

examples.text: Да перестаньте! Я двадцать лет в карты не играла.
examples.trans: Oh, stop it! I haven't played cards for twenty years.

examples.text: Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!

meanings.note: On foot, once. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.en: to sleep off drunkenness, sober up through sleep
meanings.note: Reflexive verb. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'спаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sleep off (drunkenness), sober up', paired with 'просыпаться'.

examples.trans: Go home and sleep it off properly.
In the morning he finally slept it off.
Enough making noise, go sleep it off, commander.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('drunk').

examples.text: Тогда была моя ошибка. И мы были пьяные.
examples.trans: Back then it was my mistake. And we were drunk.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

разбить.gloss: to break, to smash, to wreck (a car)

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break, to smash, to wreck (a car)', paired with 'разбивать'.

Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break, to smash, to wreck (a car)', paired with 'разбивать'.

examples.trans: Did you wreck the car or what?

examples.text: Это от руля синяк! В какой машине? Ты машину разбил, что ли?
examples.trans: That's a bruise from a steering wheel! In what car? Did you wreck the car or what?

examples.text: Я так вспоминаю. Значит, машину разбил, что ли?
examples.trans: I'm trying to recall it. So I wrecked the car, then?

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: у меня сердце = I have a bad heart (colloquial)

examples.text: Мне горько, мне плохо. У меня сердце.
examples.trans: I feel bitter, I feel awful. I have a bad heart.

meanings.note: Informal. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sit, to be sitting', paired with 'посидеть'.

examples.trans: Why are you sitting in the corner?

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Manner adverb. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Они так трогательно заботятся друг о друге.
examples.trans: They care for each other so touchingly.

meanings.note: The room or the bowl. Common masculine noun meaning 'toilet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The toilet is in the corridor.
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money
Хватит!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be enough', paired with 'хватать'.

examples.trans: Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to make noise'.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
